slot.brief: Integral that needs one application of integration by parts (log or inverse-trig times algebraic); ask the antiderivative.

stem: An antiderivative of $\displaystyle\int x\ln x\,dx$ is

verdicts.working: By parts, ∫ x ln x dx = (x²/2) ln x − ∫ x/2 dx = (x²/2) ln x − x²/4 + C.

working:
$u=\ln x,\quad dv=x\,dx$; hence $du=\dfrac{dx}{x},\quad v=\dfrac{x^2}{2}$. 
$\displaystyle\int x\ln x\,dx=\dfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\dfrac12\int x\,dx=\dfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\dfrac{x^2}{4}+C$.

Independent check: By parts, ∫ x ln x dx = (x²/2) ln x − ∫ x/2 dx = (x²/2) ln x − x²/4 + C.
solution:
Using integration by parts, take $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x\,dx$, so $du=\frac{dx}{x}$ and $v=\frac{x^2}{2}$.\\
$$\int x\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac12\int x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^2}{4}+C.$$
